steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO1: Recall knowledge and understanding (e.g. define, state, name)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO2: Apply knowledge and understanding to familiar and unfamiliar contexts (e.g. explain, describe)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO3: Analyse, evaluate and make judgements (e.g. discuss, evaluate, compare)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mathematical skills: using standard form, unit conversions, ratios, percentages and algebra

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between 'describe' and 'explain'? | Q: How should you approach a 6-mark extended writing question? | Q: Why must you show your working in calculations?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 'Describe' means state what happens (the facts). 'Explain' means say why or how it happens (the reasoning/mechanism). | 1) Read the question carefully and identify the command word. 2) Plan your answer — ensure you cover all aspects. 3) Write in structured paragraphs using scientific terminology. 4) Include relevant ex | Marks are awarded for the method/steps, not just the final answer. If you make an arithmetic error but the method is correct, you can still earn most marks.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Command words are critical: 'describe' ≠ 'explain' — know the difference Both AQA and Edexcel use AO1/AO2/AO3 marking — target each in your answers In maths questions: write the formula, substitute values, calculate, include units Extended writing: use connectives (therefore, because, however, as a result) for coherence Check your answer is reasonable — a planet's temperature of 10,000°C would be wrong for most planets
